newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO SAYS HE MIGHT LEAVE BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO SAYS HE MIGHT LEAVE BARCELONA.

text.p: World player of the year Ronaldo said on Monday the "door is open" for him to leave Barcelona at the end of the season.

"I would like to stay here but I'm a professional and I must choose what is best for me. Circumstances could make me go," said the Brazilian striker, whose representatives are pushing Barcelona for an improved contract.
Ronaldo said he felt he had a right to negotiate with other clubs because club president Jose Luis Nunez had not kept an agreement to improve his contract.
The young Brazilian was signed from Dutch side PSV Eindhoven in the close season for a then world-record fee of 2.5 billion pesetas ($17.4 million).
But several breath-taking displays led Barcelona to open negotiations over a new contract, which would in theory have raised Ronaldo's price to at least four billion pesetas ($27.8 million).
His annual pay cheque would rise from an estimated 200 million pesetas ($1.39 million) to 500 million ($3.47 million).
Despite initial indications that agreeing the new contract was a mere formality it was never signed, and Barcelona now say no new deal will be reached before the end of the season.
Ronaldo's compatriot Giovanni has asked the Barcelona board to consider an offer for him from Brazil's Sao Paulo.
The midfielder has been relegated to the bench recently and said on Monday: "I didn't come to Spain to stroll around but to triumph".
But he said he would only consider the offer to join Sao Paulo on loan if it meant he could stay there until the 1998 World Cup.
"If not I will stay in Barcelona and wait for an opportunity to arrive," said Giovanni, who has lost his place to Nou Camp favourite Ivan de la Pena.
